title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Video2DoorTraversal: Door Twin for Real-World Traversal

### The Breakthrough
The authors present Video2DoorTraversal, a pipeline that builds a simulation‑ready 3D twin of a door from a single RGB video and trains a mobile manipulator to open and traverse it. DoorTwin reconstructs an articulated door model from one video, then a simulation‑in‑the‑loop agent creates a parameterized skill program that trains ArticuACT, a dual‑depth policy predicting base, arm, and gripper commands on‑board. This enables a wheel‑legged robot to learn coordinated loco‑manipulation without manual modeling, and reported high real‑world success rates.

### The Caveats
The work provides no baseline comparison to existing door‑opening methods, so its claimed advantage remains unsubstantiated.

## MILD: Terrain-Aware Bipedal Locomotion

### The Breakthrough
MILD combines a physics‑grounded discrete‑element contact solver with latent modulation and online proprioceptive terrain estimation to train a bipedal controller via deep reinforcement learning. The resulting policy adapts online to a wide range of surface stiffnesses, demonstrating real‑robot identification and walking on deformable terrain.

### The Caveats
The paper never names or implements concrete baselines, so the purported improvement cannot be validated.

## Evidence-Gated TAMP with Vision-Language Models

### The Breakthrough
The Evidence Acquisition and Feasibility Gating (EAFG) framework interleaves vision‑language‑model‑generated exploratory actions with task‑and‑motion planning, gating execution based on feasibility. In cooking experiments with ambiguous objects, EAFG increased recipe completion by discovering relevant items before planning and safely halting when objects were missing.

### The Caveats
No baseline comparisons are provided, leaving the claimed improvement unsubstantiated.

## DECOWAM: Whole-Body Model for Legged Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
DECOWAM augments a frozen FastWAM backbone with lightweight adapters, a distilled action‑equivalent bottleneck, and split latent spaces for base and arm, trained on the ARMDOG dataset. With only 25.95 M trainable parameters it reduces action MSE by 21.7 % versus FastWAM and shows the best whole‑body coordination in 79 closed‑loop trials, matching top task‑completion rates.

### The Caveats
The strongest baseline is unnamed, so superiority beyond FastWAM remains unclear.

## Persona AI Humanoid Welding

### The Breakthrough
Persona AI is developing a bipedal humanoid equipped with a handheld welding tool to perform long, linear welds in shipyards, leveraging the robot’s precision and endurance to match or exceed human weld quality at scale.

### The Caveats
No hardware trials, performance metrics, or baseline comparisons are provided, making economic viability unsupported.

## Waymo Custom ASIC for Robotaxis

### The Breakthrough
Waymo announced a custom ASIC that integrates perception, planning, and control onto a single silicon die, aiming to cut latency and power use versus off‑the‑shelf GPUs for its next‑generation robotaxis.

### The Caveats
The announcement lacks performance metrics, baseline data, or real‑world deployment evidence.

## GEN-1.5 Robot Foundation Model

### The Breakthrough
GEN-1.5 is a large‑scale foundation model that claims one‑shot learning across robotic platforms, enabling rapid skill acquisition from a single demonstration.

### The Caveats
The claim is unsupported; the video provides no quantitative results or systematic testing.

## RoboDojo Benchmark Highlights Low Success

### The Breakthrough
Evaluation on the RoboDojo benchmark showed that 32 of 34 robot policies achieved less than 10 % success, underscoring the difficulty of current approaches on these tasks.

### The Caveats
The report gives no details on the policies or tasks, preventing assessment of significance.

## Dora: Rust Low-Latency Dataflow Middleware

### The Breakthrough
DORA is a Rust‑based framework offering zero‑copy shared‑memory IPC and Zenoh‑based transport, claiming 10‑17× lower latency than ROS2 Python and 3‑10× higher throughput for large payloads.

### The Caveats
No benchmark data or baseline comparison to ROS 2 is provided, leaving latency claims unverified.

## Agent-Worlds Multi-Agent OS

### The Breakthrough
Agent‑Worlds decouples LLM inference from game logic via a Model Context Protocol, enabling each NPC to run its own LLM wrapper and maintain dual‑tier memory for emergent social behavior in a persistent 2D pixel‑art world.

### The Caveats
The repo lacks formal evaluation or baseline comparison, so emergent capabilities remain unverified.

## Synaptic Harmony Swarm Foraging

### The Breakthrough
The repository provides a NumPy‑based simulation where multiple agents learn decentralized foraging via independent Q‑tables, supporting adaptive spatial memory in dynamic grid worlds.

### The Caveats
No quantitative evaluation or baseline is offered, so claims of emergent cooperation are unvalidated.

### Priority
Video2DoorTraversal stands out as a concrete sim‑to‑real pipeline that lets a mobile robot learn a complex door‑opening skill from a single video, offering immediate practical value for embodied AI practitioners.

### One action
Watch the accompanying video demonstration and consider replicating the DoorTwin pipeline on your own mobile platform.

### What to watch
Several papers (Video2DoorTraversal, Evidence‑Gated TAMP, and DECOWAM) explore integrating perception, language, and control for long‑horizon manipulation. Video2DoorTraversal focuses on sim‑to‑real door articulation, Evidence‑Gated TAMP adds language‑driven feasibility gating, while DECOWAM targets whole‑body coordination for legged manipulators. Together they signal a trend toward hybrid perception‑planning systems that blend learned models with symbolic reasoning.
